options.label: Game Boy Model (Restart)
options.description: Runs loaded content with a specific Game Boy model. 'Autodetect' will select the most appropriate model for the current game.

options.label: Use BIOS File if Found (Restart)
options.description: Use official BIOS/bootloader for emulated hardware, if present in RetroArch's system directory.

options.label: Skip BIOS Intro (Restart)
options.description: When using an official BIOS/bootloader, skip the start-up logo animation. This setting is ignored when 'Use BIOS File if Found' is disabled.

options.label: Default Game Boy Palette
options.description: Selects which palette is used for Game Boy games that are not Game Boy Color or Super Game Boy compatible, or if the model is forced to Game Boy.

options.label: Hardware Preset Game Boy Palettes (Restart)
options.description: Use the palettes for Game Boy games that have presets on the Game Boy Color or Super Game Boy.

options.label: Use Super Game Boy Borders (Restart)
options.description: Display Super Game Boy borders when running Super Game Boy enhanced games.

options.label: Color Correction
options.description: Adjusts output colors to match the display of real GBA/GBC hardware.

options.label: Interframe Blending
options.description: Simulates LCD ghosting effects. 'Simple' performs a 50:50 mix of the current and previous frames. 'Smart' attempts to detect screen flickering, and only performs a 50:50 mix on affected pixels. 'LCD Ghosting' mimics natural LCD response times by combining multiple buffered frames. 'Simple' or 'Smart' blending is required when playing games that aggressively exploit LCD ghosting for transparency effects (Wave Race, Chikyuu Kaihou Gun ZAS, F-Zero, the Boktai series...).

options.label: Audio Filter
options.description: Enables a low pass audio filter to reduce the 'harshness' of generated audio.

options.label: Audio Filter Level
options.description: Specifies the cut-off frequency of the low pass audio filter. A higher value increases the perceived 'strength' of the filter, since a wider range of the high frequency spectrum is attenuated.

options.label: Allow Opposing Directional Input
options.description: Enabling this will allow pressing / quickly alternating / holding both left and right (or up and down) directions at the same time. This may cause movement-based glitches.

options.label: Solar Sensor Level
options.description: Sets ambient sunlight intensity. Can be used by games that included a solar sensor in their cartridges, e.g: the Boktai series.

options.label: Game Boy Player Rumble (Restart)
options.description: Enabling this will allow compatible games with the Game Boy Player boot logo to make the controller rumble. Due to how Nintendo decided this feature should work, it may cause glitches such as flickering or lag in some of these games.

options.label: Idle Loop Removal
options.description: Reduce system load by optimizing so-called 'idle-loops' - sections in the code where nothing happens, but the CPU runs at full speed (like a car revving in neutral). Improves performance, and should be enabled on low-end hardware.

options.label: Frameskip
options.description: Skip frames to avoid audio buffer under-run (crackling). Improves performance at the expense of visual smoothness. 'Auto' skips frames when advised by the frontend. 'Auto (Threshold)' utilises the 'Frameskip Threshold (%)' setting. 'Fixed Interval' utilises the 'Frameskip Interval' setting.

options.label: Frameskip Threshold (%)
options.description: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Auto (Threshold)', specifies the audio buffer occupancy threshold (percentage) below which frames will be skipped. Higher values reduce the risk of crackling by causing frames to be dropped more frequently.

options.label: Frameskip Interval
options.description: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Fixed Interval', the value set here is the number of frames omitted after a frame is rendered - i.e. '0' = 60fps, '1' = 30fps, '2' = 15fps, etc.

options.label: Microphone Input Mode
options.description:
Choose the sound that the emulated microphone will receive:

Silence: No audio input.
Blow: Loop a built-in blowing sound.
Noise: Random white noise.
Microphone: Use your real microphone if available, fall back to Silence if not.

options.label: Microphone Button Mode
options.description:
Set the behavior of the Microphone button, even if Microphone Input Mode is set to Blow or Noise. The emulated microphone receives silence when disabled by the button.

Hold: Button enables mic input while held.
Toggle: Button enables mic input when pressed, disables it when pressed again.
Always: Button is ignored, mic input is always enabled.

Ignored if Microphone Input Mode is set to Silence.

options.label: Audio Bit Depth
options.description: The number of bits used for each audio sample. Automatic matches the original hardware's behavior by using 10-bit audio for DS mode and 16-bit audio for DSi mode. If unsure, set to Automatic.

options.label: Audio Interpolation
options.description: Interpolates audio output for improved quality. Disable this to match the behavior of the original DS hardware.

options.label: JIT Recompiler
options.description: Recompiles emulated machine code into native code as it runs, considerably improving performance over plain interpretation. Takes effect at next restart. If unsure, leave enabled.

options.label: Network MAC Address Mode
options.description:
Configures how the emulated console's MAC address is set. Changing this option might make local multiplayer impossible or block access to save files in games that use the MAC address to prevent tampering of save files (i.e. Pokémon).
No relation to the direct mode interface. Changes take effect at next restart.
See https://bit.ly/4fJtWKN for more information.

options.label: Networking Mode
options.description:
Configures how melonDS DS emulates Nintendo WFC. If unsure, use Indirect mode.

Indirect: Use libslirp to emulate the DS's network stack. Simple and needs no setup.
Direct: Routes emulated Wi-Fi packets to the host's network interface. Faster and more reliable, but requires an ethernet connection and that libpcap is installed. If unavailable, falls back to Indirect mode.

Changes take effect at next restart. Not related to local multiplayer.

options.label: Cursor Mode
options.description: Determines when a cursor should appear on the bottom screen. Never is recommended for touch screens; the other settings are best suited for mouse or joystick input.

options.label: Cursor Timeout
options.description: If Cursor Mode is set to "Until Timeout", then the cursor will be hidden if it hasn't been moved for a certain time.

options.label: Touch Mode
options.description:
Determines how the console's touch screen is emulated.

Joystick: Use a joystick to control the cursor. Recommended if you don't have a mouse or a real touch screen available.
Pointer: Use your mouse or touch screen to control the cursor.
Auto: Use either Joystick or Pointer, depending on which you last touched.

If unsure, set to Auto.

options.label: Joystick Cursor Deadzone
options.description: If the joystick is within this deadzone the cursor will not move.

options.label: Joystick Cursor Max Speed
options.description: Set the max speed for the joystick cursor.

options.label: Joystick Cursor Response
options.description:
Set the response curve for the joystick cursor.
Linear is a response curve where the cursor speed is 1:1 with the joystick input.
Quadratic is a response curve that reduces the sensitivity near the joystick center for finer control, but increases the sensitivity near the edges

options.label: Joystick Cursor Multiplier
options.description: Set the multiplier for the joystick cursor when the speedup/slowdown pointer button (L2 by default) is held

options.label: # of Screen Layouts
options.description: The number of screen layouts to cycle through with the Next Layout button.

options.label: Hybrid/Largescreen Ratio
options.description: The size of the larger screen relative to the smaller ones when using a hybrid or largescreen layout.

options.label: Hybrid Small Screen Mode
options.description: Choose which screens will be shown when using a hybrid layout.

options.label: Hybrid/Largescreen Filtering
options.description:
Affects how the hybrid/largescreen screen is scaled up.

Nearest: No filtering. Graphics look blocky.
Linear: Smooth scaling.

options.label: Screen Gap
options.description: Choose how large the gap between the screens should be. Vertical layouts (including rotations) only. Dimensions exclude the effects of the frontend's scaling.

options.label: Secondary Screen Scale
options.description: The size of the secondary screen relative to the primary screen. Applies to vertical layouts (Top/Bottom, Bottom/Top). At 100%, both screens are the same size. At 50%, the secondary screen is half the width and height of the primary screen.

options.label: Secondary Screen Filtering
options.description:
Affects how the secondary screen is scaled down.

Nearest: No filtering. Graphics look blocky.
Linear: Smooth scaling. Recommended when using Secondary Screen Scale below 100%.

options.label: DNS Override
options.description:
The DNS server to use for the emulated access point ("melonAP"). Use this to play online with custom servers that reimplement the discontinued Nintendo Wi-Fi Connection services. Game support depends on the server. 
Some internet service providers may block requests to these servers. If this is the case for you, see https://tinyurl.com/393cb755 for a workaround.

The listed servers are not affiliated with libretro, Nintendo, the melonDS team, or this core's author. Please respect other players and follow the server's rules.

If unsure, leave on Kaeru WFC. Changes take effect at next restart.

options.label: Language
options.description:
Overrides the language mode of the emulated console.

Use Host: Uses the frontend's language if supported by the console.
Don't Override: Use whatever language is already set on the firmware. This is the fallback behavior if the emulated DS (or DSi NAND) doesn't support the frontend's language.

Not every game honors this setting. Changes take effect at next restart.

options.label: Username
options.description:
Overrides the username given to the emulated console.

Don't Override: Uses whatever name is defined on the firmware.
Guess: Try to get your username from the frontend. If that fails, try the USER, USERNAME, and LOGNAME environment variables.
melonDS DS: Uses "melonDS DS". This is the default if nothing else works.

Names are truncated to 10 characters. Changes take effect at next restart.

options.label: Favorite Color
options.description: The theme ("favorite color") of the emulated console. Changes take effect at next restart.

options.label: Birth Month
options.description: The month of your birthday. Changes take effect at next restart.

options.label: Birth Day
options.description: The day within the month of your birthday. Changes take effect at next restart.

options.label: Enable Alarm
options.description: Whether the emulated console's alarm is enabled. Changes take effect at next restart.

options.label: Alarm Hour
options.description: The hour of the configured alarm. Changes take effect at next restart.

options.label: Alarm Minute
options.description: The minute of the configured alarm. Changes take effect at next restart.

options.label: Console Mode
options.description:
Whether melonDS should emulate a Nintendo DS or a Nintendo DSi. DSi mode has some limits:

- Native BIOS/firmware/NAND files must be provided, including for the regular DS.
- Some features (such as savestates) are not available in DSi mode.
- Direct boot mode cannot be used for DSiWare.

See the DSi-specific options in this category for more information. If unsure, set to DS mode unless playing a DSi game. Changes take effect at the next restart.

options.label: Slot-2 Device
options.description:
The peripheral that will be inserted into the emulated console's Slot-2. Ignored in DSi mode, or if a GBA ROM is explicitly loaded. If a GBA ROM for any game in the Boktai trilogy is inserted, the corresponding Solar Sensor setting will be forced. In supported NDS games, each Boktai cart will have different effects. 
Changes take effect at next core start.

options.label: Use Host Light Sensor
options.description:
If enabled, the emulated solar sensor's light input will come from your device's real luminance sensor if available. If disabled or no sensor is available, the emulated sensor can be manually controlled with the following button combos:

- L+A+Up or L+A+Down
- Select+Up or Select+Down
- Your mouse wheel

Ignored unless "Slot-2 Device" is set to Solar Sensor, or if a ROM for any game in the Boktai trilogy (any region) is inserted in the emulated console's Slot-2. If unsure, leave enabled.

options.label: BIOS/Firmware Mode (DS Mode)
options.description:
Determines whether melonDS uses native BIOS/firmware dumps or its own built-in replacements. Only applies to DS mode, as DSi mode always requires native BIOS and firmware dumps.

Native mode uses BIOS and firmware files from a real DS. Place your dumps of these in the system directory or its "melonDS DS" subdirectory and name them as follows:

- DS BIOS: bios7.bin, bios9.bin
- DSi BIOS: dsi_bios7.bin, dsi_bios9.bin
- Firmware: See the "DS Firmware" and "DSi Firmware" options.
- DSi NAND: See the "DSi NAND " option.

Falls back to Built-In if any BIOS/firmware file isn't found.

Built-In mode uses melonDS's built-in BIOS and firmware, and is suitable for most games.

Changes take effect at next restart.

options.label: Boot Mode
options.description:
Determines how melonDS boots games.

Native: Load games through the system menu, similar to the real DS/DSi boot process. Requires native BIOS and firmware files in the system directory.
Direct: Skip the system menu and go straight to the game. Supported for DSiWare if native DSi system files are available.

Ignored if loaded without a game (Native is forced) or if using Built-In BIOS/Firmware (Direct is forced). Changes take effect at next restart.

options.label: Read-Only Mode (DSi)
options.description: If enabled, the emulated DSi sees the virtual SD card as read-only. Changes take effect with next restart.

options.label: Sync SD Card to Host (DSi)
options.description: If enabled, the virtual SD card's files will be synced to this core's save directory. Enable this if you want to add files to the virtual SD card from outside the core. Syncing happens when loading and unloading a game, so external changes won't have any effect while the core is running. Takes effect at the next boot. Adjusting this setting may overwrite existing save data.

options.label: Read-Only Mode
options.description: If enabled, homebrew applications will see the virtual SD card as read-only. Changes take effect with next restart.

options.label: Sync SD Card to Host
options.description: If enabled, the virtual SD card's files will be synced to this core's save directory. Enable this if you want to add files to the virtual SD card from outside the core. Syncing happens when loading and unloading a game, so external changes won't have any effect while the core is running. Takes effect at the next boot. Adjusting this setting may overwrite existing save data.

options.label: Battery Update Interval
options.description: How often the emulated console's battery should be updated. Ignored if the frontend can't get the device's battery level.

options.label: DS Low Battery Threshold
options.description: If the host's battery level falls below this percentage, the emulated DS will report that its battery level is low. Ignored if running in DSi mode, no battery is available, or the frontend can't query the power status.

options.label: Time Mode
options.description:
The initial time of the emulated console's internal clock.

- Real: Start in sync with your device's clock.
- Synchronized: Synchronize the emulated clock to your device's clock. May cause unexpected behavior in some games when rewinding or fast-forwarding.
- Relative: Start in sync with your device's clock, plus or minus a specified offset. Will be constrained to dates that the DS can represent.
- Absolute: Start at a specific date and time, regardless of your device's clock.

All dates and times are in your local timezone. Changes take effect at next restart.

options.label: Starting Time Offset (Years)
options.description: The number of years to offset the starting time by. Only used when Starting Time Mode is Relative. Changes take effect at next restart.

options.label: Starting Time Offset (Days)
options.description: The number of days to offset the starting time by. Only used when Starting Time Mode is Relative. Changes take effect at next restart.

options.label: Starting Time Offset (Hours)
options.description: The number of hours to offset the starting time by. Only used when Starting Time Mode is Relative. Changes take effect at next restart.

options.label: Starting Time Offset (Minutes)
options.description: The number of minutes to offset the starting time by. Only used when Starting Time Mode is Relative. Changes take effect at next restart.

options.label: Starting Year
options.description: The initial year to use when Starting Time Mode is Absolute. Changes take effect at next restart.

options.label: Starting Month
options.description: The initial month to use when Starting Time Mode is Absolute. Changes take effect at next restart.

options.label: Starting Day
options.description: The initial day of the month to use when Starting Time Mode is Absolute. Days that extend past the end of a month will roll over to the next (e.g. April 31st will become May 1st). Changes take effect at next restart.

options.label: Starting Hour
options.description: The initial hour to use when Starting Time Mode is Absolute. Changes take effect at next restart.

options.label: Starting Minute
options.description: The initial minute to use when Starting Time Mode is Absolute. Changes take effect at next restart.

options.label: Render Mode
options.description:
Software mode is faster and more accurate, while OpenGL mode supports scaling up the resolution of 3D graphics in most cases.

OpenGL mode may be buggy on some graphics hardware. If it doesn't work, software rendering is used as a fallback. Changes take effect immediately but may require the frontend's video driver to be restarted.

options.label: Internal Resolution
options.description: The degree to which the emulated 3D engine's graphics are scaled up. Dimensions are given per screen. OpenGL renderer only.

options.label: Improved Polygon Splitting
options.description: Enable this if your game's 3D models are not rendering correctly. OpenGL renderer only.

options.label: Threaded Software Renderer
options.description: If enabled, the software renderer will run on a separate thread. Changes take effect immediately. If unsure, leave this enabled.

options.label: Warn About Unsupported Features
options.description: Enable to display an on-screen message if melonDS tries to use certain unsupported features. These warnings will be logged regardless of this setting.

options.label: Warn About Certain BIOS Problems
options.description: Enable to display warnings if your BIOS files have certain known problems. A warning will always be shown if your BIOS files are missing or invalid, regardless of this setting.

options.label: Show Screen Layout
options.description: Enable to show which screen layout within the configured sequence is active.

options.label: Show Host Microphone State
options.description: Enable to show whether your device's microphone is active.

options.label: Show Host Camera State
options.description: Enable to show whether your device's camera is active.

options.label: Show Lid State
options.description: Enable to show whether the emulated screens are closed.

options.label: Show Sensor Reading
options.description: Enable to show the emulated input of any peripheral sensors that aren't already managed by one of the other OSD options, e.g. the solar sensor embedded in the Boktai trilogy's carts. If no peripherals (including GBA carts) are available, this option will have no effect.

options.label: Enable CPU JIT
options.description: Enable Just-In-Time compilation for ARM CPU emulation. Significantly improves performance but may reduce accuracy. Restart required.

options.label: CPU Clock Speed
options.description: Adjust the emulated 3DS CPU clock speed as a percentage of normal speed. Higher values may improve performance in some games but can cause issues. Lower values can help with games that run too fast.

options.label: 3DS System Model
options.description: Select whether to emulate the original 3DS or New 3DS. New 3DS has additional CPU power and memory, required for some games. Restart required.

options.label: 3DS System Region
options.description: Set the 3DS system region. Auto-select will choose based on the game. Some games are region-locked and require matching regions.

options.label: 3DS System Language
options.description: Set the system language for the emulated 3DS. This affects in-game text language when supported.

options.label: Audio Emulation
options.description: Select audio emulation method. HLE is faster, LLE is more accurate.

options.label: Microphone Input Type
options.description: Select how microphone input is handled for games that support it.

options.label: Graphics API
options.description: Select the graphics rendering API. Auto will choose the best available option. Restart required.

options.label: Enable Hardware Shaders
options.description: Use GPU hardware to accelerate shader processing. Significantly improves performance but may reduce accuracy.

options.label: Enable Shader JIT
options.description: Use Just-In-Time compilation for shaders. Improves performance but may cause graphical issues in some games.

options.label: Accurate Shader Multiplication
options.description: Use accurate multiplication in shaders. More accurate but can reduce performance. Only works with hardware shaders.

options.label: Hardware Shader Cache
options.description: Save compiled shaders to disk to reduce loading times on subsequent runs.

options.label: Internal Resolution
options.description: Render the 3DS screens at a higher resolution. Higher values improve visual quality but significantly impact performance.

options.label: Texture Filter
options.description: Apply texture filtering to enhance visual quality. Some filters may significantly impact performance.

options.label: Texture Sampling
options.description: Control how textures are sampled and filtered.

options.label: Custom Textures
options.description: Enable loading of custom texture packs to replace original game textures.

options.label: Dump Game Textures
options.description: Save original game textures to disk for creating custom texture packs. May impact performance.

options.label: Screen Layout
options.description: Choose how the 3DS screens are arranged in the display.

options.label: Prominent 3DS Screen
options.description: Choose which screen is displayed prominently in single screen or large screen layouts.

options.label: Screen Swap Mode
options.description: How screen swapping behaves when using the screen swap hotkey.

options.label: Large Screen Proportion
options.description: How many times larger the main screen is compared to the small screen in the Large Screen layout.

options.label: Stereoscopic 3D Mode
options.description: Stereoscopic 3D output, used when a game is rendering in 3D. 'Off' shows a single 2D image. 'Side by Side' places the left and right eye images beside each other in one frame, each at half width. 'Side by Side (Full)' does the same but keeps each eye at full width. 'Anaglyph' merges both eyes into a single red/cyan image for use with red/cyan glasses. 'Interlaced' alternates the eyes on odd and even scanlines for interlaced 3D displays, and 'Reverse Interlaced' swaps which eye is on which line. 'Cardboard VR' outputs side by side with lens-distortion correction for Cardboard-style viewers.

options.label: Stereoscopic 3D Depth
options.description: Depth intensity of the stereoscopic 3D effect, as a percentage. Only used when a 3D mode is active.

options.label: Enable Virtual SD Card
options.description: Enable virtual SD card support for homebrew and some commercial games.

options.label: Save Data Location
options.description: Choose where save data and system files are stored.

options.label: Right Analog Function
options.description: Configure what the right analog stick controls.

options.label: Analog Deadzone
options.description: Set the deadzone percentage for analog input to reduce drift.

options.label: Mouse Touchscreen Support
options.description: Enable mouse input for touchscreen interactions.

options.label: Touch Device Support
options.description: Enable touch device input for touchscreen interactions.

options.label: Touch Pointer Timeout
options.description: Whether or not the touchscreen pointer should disappear during inactivity.

options.label: Gyroscope/Accelerometer Support
options.description: Enable gyroscope and accelerometer input for games that support motion controls.

options.label: Motion Sensitivity
options.description: Adjust sensitivity of motion controls (gyroscope/accelerometer).
